authors: Angelopoulos, A.N., Bates, S., Fisch, A., Lei, L. & Schuster, T.
title: Conformal risk control
relevance: Generalizes conformal prediction from coverage to controlling the expected value of ANY monotone loss - and names bounding the FALSE NEGATIVE RATE as a worked application. That is our headline complaint stated as a controllable quantity: recall .51-.78 means an FNR of .22-.49 that we currently estimate and cannot bound. CRC would instead let us CHOOSE a per-year operating threshold with a provable bound on missed canopy, from a modest in-year calibration set - turning threshold selection from a tuning decision into a guarantee. It also carries extensions for distribution shift, which is the case we actually have.

title: Conformal prediction for image segmentation using morphological prediction sets
source: MICCAI 2025, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, 78-88
relevance: Peer-reviewed segmentation-specific conformal method that conformalizes the number of morphological DILATION iterations needed to reach a target coverage, working directly on predicted and ground-truth masks. Attractive for us because the output is still a mask - it yields an inner/outer envelope around each predicted crown rather than a probability, which is closer to a per-crown validity interval than a calibrated softmax is. Gives a published, citable baseline that later preprints in this line are measured against.

authors: Andeol, L., Mossina, L., Mazoyer, A. & Gerchinovitz, S.
title: Conformal object detection by sequential risk control
relevance: Extends conformal risk control to sequential two-parameter detection tasks, with losses built for detection certification including a box-wise recall loss - the proportion of MISSED objects. Directly applicable to a per-crown deliverable: it bounds the fraction of crowns we fail to detect, per year, valid at any dataset size and without assumptions about the model or the data distribution. The 'any dataset size' property is what makes it usable at our human-sample budget where variance-limited estimation is not.

authors: Lu, K., Kluger, D.M., Bates, S. & Wang, S.
title: Conformal prediction sets for instance segmentation
relevance: Answers our open question Q10 directly: object-level conformal for instance segmentation exists, guaranteeing the probability that at least one prediction in the set has high IoU with the true instance mask, with set size adapting to query difficulty. This is the correct statistical object for per-crown validity intervals - pixel-wise coverage does not imply crown-wise coverage. Beats conformal risk control and morphological dilation baselines; note the guarantee is 'at least one prediction is good', which is weaker than 'this specific crown is right' and may need adapting before it fits our per-crown claim.
